investigation_stage: Stage-6 (Element / Output-Position & Stress Recovery Averaging Semantics)

key_scientific_resolutions.hypothesis: Visual Contour Perception vs Literal Sizing Math
key_scientific_resolutions.evidence: 97.83% of specimen elements reside in the lowest 5% colormap bracket (solid dark blue), giving the visual illusion of a narrow horizontal band in linear contour plots despite far-field background recovery noise (0.0072 MPa, ~1.09% relative error) that triggers uniform mathematical refinement under eta_req=1.0%.

The crack corridor (0.895% of mesh) contains 88.32% of total L2 energy norm error, while the far field contains 65.57% of scalar error sum. Mesh sizing based on scalar relative error causes global over-refinement, whereas energy-norm weighting strictly localizes refinement to the crack corridor.

key_scientific_resolutions.hypothesis: Output Positions and Superconvergent Patch Recovery (SPR)
key_scientific_resolutions.evidence: MISESERI is evaluated at WHOLE_ELEMENT from integration point stresses (INTEGRATION_POINT). Intra-element Gauss point stress variance in CPE4 elements averages 0.0188 MPa globally but reaches >0.5 MPa in the corridor, confirming high-gradient stress jumps as the physical driver of SPR error.
Exterior boundary elements carry only 0.058% of energy norm error with mean error of 0.0031 MPa (lower than interior far field 0.0072 MPa), demonstrating that boundary patch truncation is negligible.
